item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.32)] Qualcomm EVP, CFO & COO Palkhiwala sells $457,129 in QCOM stock

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.14)] Talon Private Wealth LLC Acquires New Position in Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. $AMD
item.description:

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.26), AMZN Bullish (+0.22)] Enphase Energy (ENPH) Stock Looks Fairly Valued Despite New Product Hopes
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.26), AMZN Bullish (+0.22)
Enphase Energy (ENPH) stock appears fairly valued based on a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model, suggesting it's slightly undervalued, despite a 76.4% price drop over five years. However, its P/E ratio indicates it's overvalued compared to its fair multiple. The company's future hinges on new products like IQ Solid-State Transformer modules for AI data centers and the IQ EV Charger 2, which could drive future cash flows and address the mixed valuation signals.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.13), NVDA Neutral (+0.11)] Kalshi stock futures plan targets Tesla and Apple shares - Bloomberg
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.13), NVDA Neutral (+0.11)
Kalshi Inc. is planning to file for regulatory approval to offer single-stock perpetual futures in the U.S., focusing on shares of Tesla, Apple, and Nvidia. The New York-based company intends to submit its application to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Securities and Exchange Commission as early as next week. If approved, these would be the first single-stock perpetual futures offered in the United States, marking a significant expansion for newer trading platforms.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.11), AMZN Neutral (+0.15)] Salesforce Enterprise AI Harness latest salvo aimed at ServiceNow
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.11), AMZN Neutral (+0.15)
Salesforce has introduced its new Enterprise AI Harness, consolidating features from six different products, to compete with ServiceNow and other vendors in managing multi-vendor AI agents. This product aims to give users more governance tools for AI agents and the data they access, addressing concerns about the "SaaSpocalypse" and the need for cross-vendor orchestration in AI environments. Salesforce views this as a strategic move to simplify and consolidate the agentic AI control layer, similar to the evolution of cloud computing.

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.03)] S&P Global downgrades Hormel Foods outlook on high leverage
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.03)
S&P Global Ratings has downgraded Hormel Foods Corp.'s outlook from stable to negative due to sustained high leverage, which has consistently been at or above 1.8x, exceeding their expectations for the company's rating. The ratings agency projects Hormel's leverage to remain near this level through fiscal 2026, with only modest improvements expected in subsequent years, falling short of previous deleveraging forecasts. This negative outlook is also influenced by contracting EBITDA margins, rising input costs, and declining organic net sales, reflecting ongoing challenges in restoring and sustaining lower leverage levels.

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.11)] An Intel-Backed Startup Says It Can Beat HBM. Is Micron’s AI Memory Boom Vulnerable?
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.11)
An Intel-backed startup, Kepler Computing, has emerged from stealth claiming its new memory architecture can outperform conventional High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and be produced with existing tools. This development poses a potential long-term challenge to Micron Technology, a significant beneficiary of the AI memory boom due to its HBM production. While Micron currently dominates the HBM market with significant customer commitments, Kepler represents a speculative threat that could normalize scarcity premiums in the future, offering Intel strategic optionality rather than immediate earnings.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.04)] Microsoft comms chief Frank Shaw to exit after nearly three decades shaping the company's message
item.description:

Shaw, 64, does not have another job lined up and plans to take a break before deciding on his next move. He was instrumental in navigating Microsoft through significant periods, including antitrust challenges, CEO transitions, and the company's recent AI push under Satya Nadella.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.46)] Accountability, oversight and AI: Inside Microsoft’s security transformation
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.46)
After enduring several high-profile cyberattacks, Microsoft launched its Secure Future Initiative (SFI) in November 2023 to transform its cybersecurity approach. The initiative emphasizes cultural change, accountability, and the integration of AI scanning tools like MDASH to identify vulnerabilities early in the development process. Microsoft is also implementing secure-by-default policies and requiring multifactor authentication for Azure, indicating a significant shift towards prioritizing security across its products and operations.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.25)] Why National Beverage Stock Dropped, Then Popped
item.description:

Sales remained flat, and profits declined nearly 17% due to elevated input costs and tariffs, which compressed profit margins. However, the stock later reversed course and was up 1.4% as of 10:30 a.m. ET.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (-0.13)] Hims & Hers Health faces class action over alleged website tracking
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (-0.13)
Hims & Hers Health is facing a class action lawsuit alleging that the company used website tracking technologies to collect and disclose consumers' sensitive health information to third parties without consent. The lawsuit claims that Hims shared this data with companies like Amplitude, Meta, and Google to boost advertising revenue, violating privacy laws and the company's own privacy policy. This complaint comes while Hims is also dealing with a Federal Trade Commission lawsuit over alleged deceptive billing practices.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.11)] Alphabet vs. Meta: One Magnificent Seven Stock Is the Better Buy
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.11)
This article compares the Q2 2026 performances of Alphabet (GOOG) and Meta Platforms (META), two "Magnificent Seven" stocks. It concludes that Alphabet is a better buy due to its explosive cloud growth, lower valuation, and strong financial health, while Meta faces challenges from escalating capital expenditures and unresolved litigation, despite its robust advertising revenue. Alphabet's full-stack AI strategy and expanding margins are highlighted as key advantages over Meta's more concentrated and financially strained AI bets.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.35)] Why Apple’s next computer should be for the smart home
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.35)
The article argues that Apple's next significant computer should be an "intelligent home hub" to address the shortcomings of current smart home infrastructure. This device would combine a Wi-Fi router, an AI-powered smart home hub, and local storage into a single unit, prioritizing local processing for improved speed, privacy, and reliability. The author suggests this "Apple Home Server" could integrate Apple's past ventures in networking and media streaming with its current leadership in Matter and Thread protocols, providing a robust, user-friendly solution for managing digital life and smart home automations locally.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.14), NVDA Bullish (+0.28)] Jensen Huang Mocks Nvidia ‘Circular Financing’ Fears: ‘If That Is, Let’s Do More of That’
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.14), NVDA Bullish (+0.28)
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed concerns about the company's "circular financing" strategy, where it invests in AI labs and cloud providers that subsequently use Nvidia technology. Huang stated that Nvidia's capital input is small compared to the business generated, emphasizing the company's strong visibility into these projects. Skeptics, including Jim Chanos and Michael Burry, argue that this strategy blurs the lines between genuine demand and demand created by Nvidia's own financial backing.

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.12)] $6 diesel should benefit Tesla's trucking ambitions, Morgan Stanley says
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.12)
Surging diesel prices, which have surpassed $6 a gallon, could significantly boost the demand for Tesla's electric semi-trucks, according to Morgan Stanley analysts. An autonomous electric semi is projected to cut costs by 20% per mile and increase annual mileage by 133% compared to human-operated diesel vehicles. This could lead to a dramatic increase in profit per truck, making Tesla's trucking solution more attractive amidst rising fuel costs.

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.13)] Seoul And SEALSQ Build Center For Post-quantum Chip Security
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.13)
Seoul and SEALSQ Corp are partnering to establish a research and design center in Seoul focused on securing semiconductor chips against future quantum cyberattacks. The initiative, backed by a $136 million commitment from the Seoul Metropolitan Government, aims to integrate post-quantum cryptography at the semiconductor level using RISC-V architectures and NIST guidelines. This collaboration seeks to bolster South Korea's dominance in the global semiconductor market and position it as a leader in post-quantum security for both terrestrial and space-based infrastructure.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.30)] Jensen Huang Mocks Nvidia ‘Circular Financing’ Fears: ‘If That Is, Let’s Do More of That’
item.description:

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (-0.15)] How AI and cybersecurity are reshaping ServiceNow

This move positions ServiceNow to defend against the perceived "SaaS apocalypse" and compete in an AI-converged landscape, though it also introduces new competitive dynamics and potential challenges for customers.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.13)] BofA Strategists Warn of Stock Volatility as Outflows Hit US
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.13)
Bank of America strategists are warning of increased stock market volatility due to significant outflows from US equities and investor complacency regarding rising Treasury yields. US equity funds have seen $14.2 billion in outflows over three weeks, the largest since January, signaling investor caution despite a lack of widespread panic. The strategists point to "blasé markets" and "bravado policy" as a recipe for instability, citing factors like monetary policy uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and doubts about AI's economic impact.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.43)] Switch to Verizon and get the new iPhone 18 Pro now. No trade-in needed. And get the latest iPhone every year.
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.43)
Verizon is offering the new iPhone 18 Pro with no trade-in required and the option to upgrade to the latest iPhone every year through its Simplicity plan. Customers can also get additional Apple products like the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirPods 5, and the new foldable iPhone Duo. The announcement highlights Verizon's loyalty program, which includes no activation or upgrade fees and Verizon Dollars cash back.

item.description:

Following the sale, she directly owns 34,352 shares. Apple shares are trading near their 52-week high and are considered overvalued by InvestingPro, despite the recent introduction of a new foldable iPhone model, the Duo.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (-0.14)] Microsoft plans 38 gigawatts of data center capacity by 2032, Bloomberg News reports
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (-0.14)
Microsoft intends to significantly expand its data center capacity to 38 gigawatts by 2032, more than tripling its current footprint of 12 gigawatts, according to a Bloomberg News report. A growing portion of this expansion, about one-third, will be dedicated to AI-specific chips, reflecting the massive computing power required for generative AI services. The company expects substantial capital expenditures, with plans to spread long-term data center leases over 25 years to lower annual reported costs.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.32)] Amkor will expand investments in its advanced packaging facility in Arizona to $12 billion
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.32)
Amkor Technology Inc. is significantly expanding its investment in an advanced packaging and testing facility in Arizona, increasing it from $2 billion to $12 billion. This expansion will nearly triple the facility's size to over a million square feet, supporting the U.S. government's initiative to onshore advanced manufacturing. Apple is slated to be the first customer, utilizing Amkor for packaging chips produced by TSMC in Arizona.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.23)] Apple is walking a ‘tightrope’ when it comes to the prices of its new iPhones
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.23)
Apple is facing a pricing dilemma for its new iPhones, including the iPhone 18 Pro line and its first foldable phone, the Duo. Analysts suggest the company may need to absorb some costs to maintain sales amidst rising inflation and constrained consumer spending. The challenge lies in balancing increased production costs with consumers' limited ability to pay higher prices for new devices.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.08)] BofA Tweaks Apple Stock Price Target After Ternus Debut
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.08)
Bank of America maintained its Buy rating on Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) but lowered its price target from $380 to $370 after CEO John Ternus's first product event. The adjustment reflects softer-than-expected new iPhone pricing, which could boost sales volume but pressure gross margins due to rising component costs. Despite increased iPhone unit estimates for 2026 and 2027, the reduced average selling prices led to lower profit expectations, although confidence in Apple's long-term strategy remains strong, particularly with the introduction of the foldable iPhone Duo and advancements in AI and privacy.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.01)] The Apple Watch Got a Massive AI Upgrade—and the Controversy Could Get It Banned at the Office
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.01)
The new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 feature advanced AI capabilities like Live Rewind and Siri Recap, which record and summarize conversations. While Sound Recognition offers useful accessibility features, the Live Rewind and Siri Recap functionalities raise significant privacy concerns for corporate environments. Companies may consider banning these devices in meetings due to the risk of business secrets leaking.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.12)] QYLD ETF Explained: How an $8.3 Billion Covered Call Strategy Delivers 12% Monthly Income
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.12)
The QYLD ETF utilizes a covered call strategy on the Nasdaq 100 Index to generate monthly income, boasting an $8.3 billion AUM and a 12.21% trailing twelve-month distribution yield. While it aims for current income, investors should note that this strategy caps upside potential in exchange for regular distributions from option premiums. The fund's holdings mirror the Nasdaq 100, and its performance is tied to the index's direction and volatility.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.46)] Apple catches up in foldables. Wall Street likes it
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.46)
Apple has unveiled its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, priced from $1,999, entering a market previously dominated by Samsung, Google, and Huawei. Analysts are largely positive, with Bank of America seeing a larger market opportunity and UBS expecting Apple to sell over 5 million foldable units in fiscal 2026. This launch also marks new CEO John Ternus's first major product introduction, emphasizing Apple's focus on integrated hardware, software, and services.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.11)] Skyworks Solutions Surges 10%, Qorvo Climbs 6% While Chip Stocks Fall: Is the Merger Finally Clearing?
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.11)
Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) and Qorvo (QRVO) saw significant stock surges of 10% and 6% respectively, while the broader semiconductor market experienced a decline. This divergence suggests that the market is pricing in increased optimism for their proposed merger, as Skyworks' CEO Phil Brace previously indicated the China review had entered its final phase with a target close by year-end. Investors are closely watching for formal regulatory decisions or merger-completion disclosures as the transaction appears to be nearing its conclusion.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.44)] Taiwan Semiconductor September Revenue Surges 53% and Can’t Keep Up With Demand
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.44)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) reported a 53% year-over-year surge in August 2026 revenue, reaching $16.35 billion, significantly exceeding its own full-year guidance. Despite this strong financial performance, TSMC is struggling to meet customer demand, particularly due to tight packaging capacity and a significant gap between demand and supply for AI chips. The company is aggressively expanding its capacity, with 20 fabs under construction, and anticipates continued strong demand from the AI sector through 2029-2030.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.82)] World’s largest contract chipmaker TSMC sees August revenue surge over 53% to record high
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.82)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) reported a record monthly revenue for August, surging over 53% year-on-year to $16.35 billion, primarily driven by robust demand for chips used in artificial intelligence applications. The company has maintained its dominant market share in the global foundry market, with strong bookings for its advanced chipmaking capacities. TSMC also announced a collaboration with ASML to advance next-generation chipmaking technology, planning to use ASML's High NA technology for advanced nodes starting in 2030.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.19)] Intel Climbs 5% on High-NA EUV Production Lead, ASML and Taiwan Semiconductor Advance 3%
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.19)
Intel's stock surged 5% after the company announced a lithography milestone, processing over one million wafers on High-NA EUV equipment, including production layers for its Panther Lake processors, putting it years ahead of rivals like Samsung and TSMC in this advanced technology. ASML and Taiwan Semiconductor also saw gains of 3-4% due to AI-driven demand and Intel's achievement. Intel's Q2 revenue rose 25%, marking its strongest growth in over 15 years, though its significant year-to-date gain already reflects high investor optimism.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.50)] ASML and TSMC Announce Initiative to Pioneer Industry Transition to Large-Format Photomasks for High NA EUV
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.50)
ASML and TSMC have announced a collaborative initiative to drive the semiconductor industry's transition to 12-inch photomasks for High NA EUV lithography. This move aims to increase fab productivity, lower chipmaking costs, and remove stitching constraints, enabling more cost-effective advanced chips. The initiative plans for a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031, with full lithography system readiness for advanced node production by 2033.

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.03)] Why Taiwan’s Silicon Shield Is Failing
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Neutral (+0.03)
Taiwan's "silicon shield," stemming from its dominance in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, is facing challenges as China invests heavily in chip self-reliance, particularly in mature-node chips. While Taiwan still holds leverage in cutting-edge chips, China's increasing capacity in 28-nanometer chips threatens to make Taiwan's shield irrelevant for its own economy, potentially leading to a more fragile global trade environment with rising chip prices. This shift means that the geopolitical importance of Taiwan's chip production will no longer solely rely on the most advanced technologies, but also on the control of common chip manufacturing.

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.03)] Where Does AMD Make Its Processors?
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Neutral (+0.03)
AMD processors are primarily manufactured in Taiwan by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest semiconductor producer. While TSMC has facilities in Arizona for some AI chips, the final assembly and packaging of AMD CPUs occur in places like Penang, Malaysia, and China. This manufacturing strategy is similar to Nvidia's, with TSMC also producing chips for other major tech companies like Apple and Tesla.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.50)] Marvell Technology and Taiwan Semiconductor are No-Brainer Picks: They Have What Wins in a Gold Rush
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.50)
Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) are presented as strong investment opportunities in the AI infrastructure buildout, likened to selling "picks and shovels" during a gold rush. Both companies reported impressive Q2 revenue growth (around 36%), with TSMC demonstrating broad market exposure through its foundry services and Marvell focusing on custom silicon and optical interconnects for hyperscalers. While TSMC offers a steadier investment due to its foundational role in chip manufacturing, Marvell, despite being higher-variance, shows significant growth potential, particularly with its custom silicon business projected to more than double by fiscal 2028.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.89)] TSMC will invest an additional $100 billion into Arizona operations

The investment aims to create tens of thousands of high-paying jobs and strengthen the U.S. semiconductor supply chain, driven by the surging demand for artificial intelligence.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.47)] TSM Rides on AI, Advanced Nodes & Capacity Expansion: Worth a Buy?
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.47)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) is poised for continued growth driven by the surging demand for AI infrastructure, rapid adoption of advanced process technologies, and expanding global manufacturing capacity. The company reported strong Q2 2026 revenues and expects continued robust demand, especially with the industry's shift towards agentic AI. TSM's leadership in leading-edge nodes like 3nm and the upcoming 2nm and A16 technologies, coupled with international capacity expansions, are strengthening its competitive position and addressable market opportunities.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.45)] TSMC Stock And 2 Global Blue Chips For AI Infrastructure Growth
item.description:

item.title: [TSM Bearish (-0.32)] Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd Stock (TSM) Moved Down by 3.11% on Aug 24: Facts Behind the Movement
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bearish (-0.32)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (TSM) stock declined by 3.11% on August 24, primarily due to investor profit-taking after a significant rally in the semiconductor sector, exacerbated by concerns over heavy capital expenditures and valuation. Technical indicators show a MACD sell signal and an oversold Williams %R, while fundamental analysis highlights substantial revenue and net profit figures within the Technology Equipment industry. Key risks include surging capital expenditure, valuation premia, geopolitical concentration, and operational complexities from international expansion.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.47)] Unbreakable Shield: Why Taiwan’s Chip Expertise Cannot Be Cloned
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.47)
Taiwan's semiconductor industry is a complex ecosystem, far beyond just wafer foundries, encompassing advanced packaging, materials, and a dense network of suppliers and talent. While Taiwan is building new semiconductor plants in the US, Japan, and Europe, this diversification alone will not eliminate global reliance on the island. The article argues that instead of trying to replace Taiwan, the US and Europe should focus on reinforcing Taiwan's resilience and role as a core pillar of the democratic semiconductor alliance by supporting its advancements and aligning industrial policies.
